name: Shadowfriends
body:
Long ago, a legendary knight stripped naked and took a bath in an isolated forest. He was caught by a group of bandits, who, though far from his equals in a fair fight, were able to kill him after a short scuffle. They took his weapons and armor, and left his body for the crows to find. None of this is important save one detail: They missed a particular ring in his possession.

Decades later, a runaway half-orc stumbled upon the knight’s skeletal remains. She was but a child, and scared out of her wits after escaping an abusive master, but the skeleton did not much frighten her. It was clean and grinning—almost friendly in the starlight, after the ordeal she’d been through. She named it Ribs, and slept next to it for the next few weeks. The pond was a source of water, and apples grew nearby, allowing her to survive the summer and autumn months in relative comfort. For the first time in her life, she was safe and free. But she was lonely.

And one day, while polishing the pretty ruby ring she’d found—which seemed to be missing two of its stones—she made a wish for some friends…

Physical Description: Shadowfriends are hulking, but physically frail—almost skeletal. Some can stand over thirteen feet tall, while others take more bestial shapes, resembling scrawny bears, horses, or panthers. They are charcoal-black in color, and disturbingly silent when they walk; they weigh only about 60 pounds. Many choose not to talk, or speak very rarely.

Society: Shadowfriends rarely like to associate with others of their kind, and seem pained when they must do so. They generally wander the wilderness alone, looking for travelers who need assistance—particularly children. Others stalk towns, protecting the young folk from abusive homes and employers. Being born from a ring of wishes, shadowfriends have no other means of reproduction, and every year their numbers dwindle. Not even they are exactly certain how many of their kind exist in the world these days.

Relations: Dwarves treat shadowfriends with hefty suspicion, and shadowfriends return the sentiment. Something about dwarves tends to set shadowfriends on edge. Elves and shadowfriends see each other as fellow guardians of the forest. Shadowfriends often mistake halflings and gnomes for children, and are somewhat perplexed by the worldly halflings (halflings find this sort of entertaining, while gnomes like to play along, seeing shadowfriends as fascinating mysteries). Shadowfriends are regarded by humans as dangerous fey to be avoided, appeased, or killed, so shadowfriends try not to be seen by humans. Shadowfriends are very kind towards half-elves and half-orcs. After so much unwanted attention, these mixed breeds see shadowfriends as a little bit patronizing, but mostly just terrifying.

What can be most disturbing to adults is the fact that very young children do not regard shadowfriends as frightening at all. In fact, they tend to be drawn to the fearsome figures, even following them into the woods on occasion. This has given the shadowfriends a reputation in some communities as child abductors and brainwashers. In truth, the shadowfriends are perfectly kind to the children, and always return them home when they are finished playing—indeed, the greatest harm comes from the fact that as the children grow older, they tend to develop a fear of their former playmates, which always hurts the shadowfriends immensely.

Alignment and Religion: Shadowfriends are kindly and protective, but can show a disturbing, even monstrous side when facing those who would harm the innocent, and so tend towards true neutral slightly more often than neutral good. They have no religion, but when asked for a being they revere, shadowfriends universally look down and say, very quietly, “Zeljka.”

Core Traits (15 RP)
Ability Score Modifiers: Shadowfriends are quick and dexterous, but their sticklike forms are frail and weak for their size. They gain +2 Dexterity, –2 Constitution, –2 Strength. –2 RP
Type: Shadowfriends are fey creatures. 2 RP
Size: Shadowfriends are Large creatures and take a –1 size penalty to their AC, a –1 size penalty on attack rolls, a +1 bonus on combat maneuver checks and to their CMD, and a –4 size penalty on Stealth checks. 7 RP
Speed: Shadowfriends have a base speed of 30 feet. They also have a climb speed of 20 feet. 2 RP
Languages: Shadowfriends begin play speaking Common and Orc. Shadowfriends with high Intelligence scores can choose from among the following bonus languages: Dwarven, Elven, Gnome, Halfling, and Sylvan.
Other Traits
Hide-and-Seek: Shadowfriends gain a +8 racial bonus on Stealth checks (+12 in forests) and Stealth is always a class skill for them. 7 RP
Trinkets: Shadowfriends gain a +2 racial bonus on checks for either Craft (toys) or Craft (clothing), chosen at character creation. Once per hour as a standard action, a shadowfriend can create one mundane object worth less than 1 gp out of shadow, provided they succeed at the appropriate Craft check. This item melts into smoke after an hour. 2 RP
Reach: Shadowfriends have a reach of 10 feet. 1 RP
Low-Light Vision: Shadowfriends can see twice as far as a race with normal vision in conditions of dim light.
Light Blindness: Abrupt exposure to bright light blinds shadowfriends for 1 round; on subsequent rounds, they are dazzled as long as they remain in the light. –2 RP
Summer’s End: Shadowfriends become torpid in cold environments, frosting over and becoming lethargic. A shadowfriend has vulnerability to cold, and automatically fails any Fortitude saves made to avoid nonlethal damage from cold environments. A shadowfriend that would otherwise be killed by exposure to cold weather instead enters permanent unconsciousness. It does not heal naturally until it is brought into a warmer area or the weather changes. –2 RP
Alternate Racial Traits

The following racial traits may be selected instead of existing shadowfriend traits.

Animal Shape: Some shadowfriends are shaped more like bizarre beasts than stretched people. They gain a +4 racial bonus to CMD against trip attempts and increase their base speed to 40 feet. They may pick two of the following natural attacks, with damage noted in parentheses: gore (1d8), slam (1d8), 2 claws (1d4), and bite (1d8). They cannot take both slam and claws. These are primary attacks. They cannot wield normal weapons, and armor is priced like barding. They do not gain reach or a climb speed.
Blend In: While in forest terrains, the shadowfriend can always attempt a Stealth check, even if it lacks concealment or cover, as long as it is not being observed and does not move. Shadowfriends with this trait do not have a climb speed.
Darkvision: Some shadowfriends are especially keyed to the shadows, and rely on them to survive. They can see perfectly in darkness out to 60 feet. Shadowfriends with this trait take 1 point of Constitution damage after every hour they are exposed to direct sunlight.
Recently Awoken: While all shadowfriends originate from the same wish, a few have been stuck in torpor in cold environments for very long periods of time, only recently reawakening. These shadowfriends have an unshakable sluggishness to them, resulting in a –4 penalty on Initiative checks. However, they are more resistant to low temperatures and freezing. The recently awoken do not have cold vulnerability nor do they automatically fail Fortitude saves against cold weather. Cold weather that would result in death still sends them into torpor. This replaces summer’s end.
